items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: The interviewee (Scott Yanow) does not mention Gary Giddins; the mention is made by the Interviewer, and the Interviewee responds to the Interviewer's question about Giddins without indicating a personal relationship.

ctx.x: Pretty even, really. When you are a jazz critic you have to know that if a musician compliments you that means if you liked their last record. That means if they say you are a great writer that means you wrote a great review for them. And if you wrote a negative review then you’re a bum. Like, so you can’t really take their opinions too seriously, much of the time, unless it’s someone you know and they’re being really honest about it. I mean it’s kind of funny, there was one saxophonist who because of the…

I recall doing an interview with a wonderful guy, a veteran trombonist. And I happened to bring up something that Gary Giddins wrote. And he immediately said, “Does he play anything? Has he ever played anything?” Like he didn’t even let me finish my sentence, it was like that was the hurdle for him in order to give some kind of credence to what Gary wrote. Had he played something. Do you think that’s important?

Yeah it’s important for a jazz critic to have as much knowledge as possible, and if you play a little bit of music that’s good. But it’s not necessary. I mean Whitney Balliet, the best of all writers on jazz, he was always my favorite. You could read his reviews and you could almost hear the music of the people he’s writing about. And I think he played drums a little bit but he didn’t really play music very often. It’s not necessary at all. I mean if it’s musicians reviewing musicians it’s going to be an obvious…
